column2: Divide into ovenproof bowls; set the bowls in a tray with water poured into it.
Divide into ovenproof bowls; set the bowls in a tray with water poured into it.
Bring plenty of water to the boil in a large pan and salt it; add the pasta and stir for the first minute so it doesn't stick.
Grate the tomatoes and crush the garlic.
Taste 1 minute before the packet time; when slightly firm, save a ladle of the cooking water and drain.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and stir the crushed garlic for 30 seconds without burning it.
Add the grated tomato and a little salt; cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens.
Add the basil and cook for 1 more minute.
Add the pasta to the sauce; if too thick, loosen with the reserved water and toss for 1 minute.
Wash the basil leaves and dry them well.
Blend the basil, walnuts, garlic, oil and a pinch of salt in a food processor into a thick sauce.
Put the sauce in a large bowl and loosen with 2–3 spoonfuls of hot pasta water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce; scatter the cheese and serve immediately.
Chop the onion finely and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and sauté over high heat for 6–8 minutes until they release and then lose their liquid.
Add the garlic and stir for 1 minute; season with salt.
Add the pasta and the reserved pasta water and toss for 1 minute.
Boil the noodles in salted boiling water for the packet time until soft; drain.
Cut the carrot, courgette and pepper into thin strips.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and sauté the carrot first for 3 minutes.
Add the pepper and courgette and sauté for 5–7 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Add the noodles and a little salt and stir for 2 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; grease the ovenproof dish.
Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the packet time so it stays firm, then drain; it will keep cooking in the oven.
Stir half the cheese into the sauce until melted.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and spread in the ovenproof dish.
Scatter the remaining cheese and bake for 20–25 minutes until golden on top.
Dice the courgette and carrot small; grate the tomato.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the carrot for 3 minutes, then add the courgette and sauté for 4 minutes.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white all over.
Chop the pepper small, add it and soften for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the hot water and a little salt; cook covered over low heat for 10–12 minutes until the noodles are soft and the water absorbed.
Tear the basil by hand, add it and serve.
Peel the pumpkin and remove the seeds; cut into large 4–5 cm cubes.
Arrange the pumpkin in the pan and sprinkle the sugar over it; leave for 1 hour to release its juice.
Add the water; cook covered over low heat for 30–40 minutes until the pumpkin is soft and has absorbed its syrup.
Test with the tip of a knife: if it goes in easily, the fruit is soft.
Leave to cool in the pan; if moved while hot it falls apart.
Transfer the pumpkin to a serving plate.
When serving, drizzle tahini and crushed walnuts over the top.
Whisk the milk, semolina and sugar together in the pan while cold so it doesn't go lumpy.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly so it doesn't catch, for 8–10 minutes until it falls slowly from the spoon.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla and butter.
Pour the mixture into an ovenproof dish or bowls.
Bake on the top shelf for 10–15 minutes until lightly coloured.
Once at room temperature, cover and chill in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Grate the tomatoes; crumble the cheese.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the tomato for 6–7 minutes until some of the liquid has evaporated.
Wash the pears and halve them; scoop out the cores with a spoon.
Sprinkle with cinnamon; add the water to the bottom of the dish.
Let cool slightly and serve with walnuts.
Dice the tomatoes and crush the garlic.
Add the tomatoes and a little salt and cook for 8–10 minutes until soft and saucy.
Add the chopped basil and serve.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the mushrooms; sauté over high heat for 6–8 minutes until they release and then lose their liquid.
Add the crushed garlic and stir for 30 seconds; season with salt.
Bring the yoghurt to room temperature and whisk with 2 spoonfuls of pasta water so it doesn't split.
Turn off the heat; add the pasta and yoghurt and toss quickly.
Wash the rice and put it in the pan with the water; simmer over low heat for 15–20 minutes until it absorbs the water and is very soft.
Add the milk and bring to the boil, stirring so it doesn't catch.
Add the sugar and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Dissolve the starch in half a glass of cold water or milk; add it to the pan while stirring.
Stir constantly for 5 minutes until thickened.
Grill at 220°C on the top rack for 10–15 minutes until browned on top, watching it closely.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease the ovenproof dish.
Cook the noodles 2 minutes less than the packet time so they stay firm, then drain.
Whisk the milk, egg and crumbled white cheese.
Put the noodles in the dish and toss with the sauce; dot the butter over the top in small pieces.
Scatter the grated kashar cheese.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the egg sauce is fully set and the top is golden.
Wash the quinces and rub off the fuzz; halve them with the skin on.
Scoop out the cores with a spoon; you can put the seeds in the bottom of the dish for colour.
Arrange the quinces cut side up in the dish and divide the sugar over them.
Add the water, cinnamon and cloves; cover with foil.
Bake for 45–60 minutes; uncover and bake for 10 more minutes until the syrup thickens.
Grate the courgettes and squeeze lightly.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the courgette for 6–7 minutes until the liquid evaporates; season with salt.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and a little salt until smooth; let it come to room temperature so it doesn't split on hot pasta.
Toss the noodles with the courgette and transfer to a serving plate.
Pour the yoghurt over the top.
Sizzle the dried mint in a little oil for 10 seconds and drizzle over.
Finely grate the orange zest without reaching the white pith.
Remove from the heat and stir in the orange zest and butter.
Wash the pears and cut in half; scoop out the cores with a spoon.
Arrange cut side up in the ovenproof dish; add 2 spoonfuls of water to the bottom.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and bake for 25–30 minutes.
Once cooled slightly, drizzle with honey and scatter the walnuts.
Honey must not be given to babies under 1 year; set aside the baby's portion without honey.
Heat the oil in a pan and soften the carrot for 4–5 minutes; season with salt.
Toss the warm pasta with the carrot; add the yoghurt and mix.
Soak the sun-dried tomatoes in hot water for 10 minutes to soften; drain and chop finely.
Add the sun-dried tomatoes and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the pasta and 3–4 spoonfuls of cooking water and toss; use less salt as sun-dried tomatoes are salty.
Add the basil and serve.
Peel the pumpkin and remove the seeds; cut into large cubes.
Cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Wash the apple and chop it small.
Soften in a pan with 2 spoonfuls of water for 3–4 minutes; add half the cinnamon and let cool.
Sprinkle with the remaining cinnamon and serve right away so the oats don't go soft.
Peel and grate the apples; mix with cinnamon right away so they don't brown.
Layer the semolina and apple in small ovenproof dishes, finishing with apple on top.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and cool for 10 minutes; the inside is very hot.
Heat the oil in a pan and sauté the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the cooked lentils and heat for 3 minutes; season with salt.
Divide the semolina pudding into bowls.
Decorate with the pear.
Heat the oil in the pan and cook the tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the noodles and cooked lentils and stir.
Add the hot water and a little salt; cook covered over low heat for 12–15 minutes until the noodles are soft.
Remove from the heat and rest for 5 minutes.
Peel and grate the apples; toss with cinnamon right away so they don't brown.
Bake for 10 minutes.
Grate the carrot; add it with the orzo and toast for 3 minutes.
Add the hot water and a little salt; cook covered over low heat for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the lemon juice and remove from the heat; leave covered for 5 minutes.
Soften in a pan with 2–3 spoonfuls of water for 5–6 minutes; add the cinnamon.
Spoon the warm apples over the yoghurt.
Add the oats, tahini and cocoa and knead; if too soft, add 1–2 more spoonfuls of oats.
Chill the mixture in the fridge for 10 minutes; it will be easier to shape.
With wet hands roll into walnut-sized balls.
Roll them in the desiccated coconut.
Rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.
They keep in a covered container in the fridge for 3 days.
Wash the pears, chop small and divide among ovenproof dishes.
Spread the mixture over the pears.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until lightly golden on top.
Drizzle with honey while warm.
Mix the pear and walnuts.
Keeps in a covered container in the fridge for 2 days.
Mix the pumpkin and walnuts.
If the plums are very sour, you can add 1 teaspoon of honey or grape molasses.
Mix half the almonds into the mixture and scatter the other half on top after filling the dishes; they toast lightly in the oven.
Feel with your fingers to make sure no stones remain; this matters for young children.
If the dates are hard, soak in warm water for 10 minutes to soften.
Add the cocoa and stir until no lumps remain.
